findings.title: The pre-registered M* decision rule cannot fire: no G14@BLUP20 inner score is ever recorded, so M* is always G14@BLUP20
findings.detail: PRE_REGISTRATION.md section 4 says the claim-carrying arm is NNC@SELECTED iff its inner k=3 score beats G14@BLUP20's inner score on a majority of BP (seed, fold) selections. decide_mstar (scripts/g20_report.py:50-74) looks for a key starting with 'G14@BLUP20' in selection['scores'], but select_on_inner (gen20k/runner.py:80-129) only writes keys 'RIDGE2@lam*' and 'NNC[<cfg>]@<mech>...' (lines 96, 110-120); the G14 arm fitted at line 91 is used only for the ridge prior and never scored. Hence g14 is always None, wins stays 0, and line 72 returns 'G14@BLUP20' unconditionally. Reproduction: read runner.py:88-129 for the key set, or run select_on_inner on any fold and list rec['scores'] keys. In addition g20_report.py:24 exposes --mstar, letting the registered arm be set by hand at report time after the outer tables exist.
findings.consequence: P1-P4 are always computed on G14@BLUP20 regardless of NNC's inner performance; if NNC@SELECTED should have been M*, every registered contrast (and the confirmation run, which takes the same M* via g20_reproduce.sh:20-21) tests the wrong arm, and the pre-registration describes a selection that the code does not perform.
findings.fix: In select_on_inner add rec['scores']['G14@BLUP20'] = _ladder_mae(bench, iva, lambda ci, sup: AD.blup(g14.curves([ci])[0], ref_cov.cov, sup, CV.noise_matrix(sup.pairs, s2)), ref_cov.cov, s2) (same supports, same covariance) and have decide_mstar read that key; remove the --mstar override from g20_report.py (keep it only in g20_confirm.py, fed from the recorded decision) and add a test that a synthetic selection record with NNC < G14 at k=3 yields NNC@SELECTED.

findings.title: The no-closure rule prevents per-pair closure only; 25 % (C3, k=3) and 76 % (C10, k=10) of the adjacent-query degrees of freedom are still exactly fixed by the supports
findings.detail: closed_pairs/assert_no_closure (design.py:107-126) are correct and sufficient for a single query pair: in a support forest, e_a-e_b lies in the row space of the incidence matrix iff a and b are connected, and the bipartite lookahead (design.py:83-142) provably lets every policy reach k_max (verified: 0 short sequences over all 378 cells, all policies, 5 random draws). But linear combinations of queries are determined. Counter-example that passes assert_no_closure: cell with metals {La, Ce, Pr}, queries La/Ce and Ce/Pr, support La/Pr (the WIDEST pick) -> y(La/Ce)+y(Ce/Pr) = support exactly (synthetic check: 1.300 == 1.300). Real cells: 0f09c750ad725e62 (La,Ce,Pr,Eu,Er; WIDEST k=3 supports La/Er, Pr/Er, La/Eu) fixes 1 of 2 query dof; the 14-metal cell at k=10 fixes 9 of its 12 query dof (k=3: 2, k=5: 4, k=8: 7). Over the cohorts with WIDEST supports: C1/k=1 51 of 2067 query dof fixed (2 %), C3/k=3 490 of 1980 (25 %), C10/k=10 992 of 1297 (76 %); 298 of 378 cells have at least one fixed combination at k_max. IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:16-17 and PRE_REGISTRATION.md section 3 state that every scored query is 'algebraically independent of the supports', which is false in this joint sense, and the gen15 'closed fraction' accounting (g20_replicate_gen15.py) counts only per-pair closure.
findings.consequence: P2 (ΔMAE k=3 vs 0), P3 (ΔR² k=3 vs 0) and P4 (k=10) will be dominated by subtraction, not by any model: at k=10 only ~3 of 12 adjacent values per 14-metal cell are free, so R²(10) is high and ΔR² 'excludes 0' for any arm that respects the support constraints, and the sealed pre-registration would carry a guarantee the design does not provide. Direction: P2/P3/P4 are inflated in favour of 'measurements make adjacent SFs predictable'.
findings.fix: Before sealing: (1) reword the pre-registration to 'no single query pair is determined' and record per (cohort, k) the fixed-dof fraction (rank([D_sup; D_q]) - rank(D_sup) free dof) in the cohort table; (2) add a label-free arithmetic null that exactly respects the support constraints with no corpus (e.g. the minimum-norm centred curve consistent with the supports, = BLUP with cov=I and R->0) and register P2/P3 against it (or against FLAT@BLUP20) rather than against k=0; (3) optionally score a 'free-component' metric by projecting query residuals onto the orthogonal complement of the support row space per cell.

findings.title: Inner selection scores inner-validation cells with a covariance that pooled those same cells' residuals
findings.detail: run_fold builds ref = covs['G14'] from fold_covariance over the whole training fold (runner.py:140-143; cov.py:67-82, 114-123) and passes it to select_on_inner (line 144). inner_oof_curves deals the training fold with inner_seed(fold.seed, fold.fold); its first inner fold is exactly fold.inner_validation_index (verified True on all 5 BP folds, seed 104729), so iva's own out-of-fold residual rows are in the pool used to (a) choose DOPT_Q supports for iva cells (runner.py:71, 110-120) and (b) run BLUP20 on iva cells (line 112). Pool share from iva: 14 % (fold 0), 9 %, 9 %, 12 %, 4 %. Measured on BP seed 104729 with G14 fitted on the masked inner-train: inner BLUP20 MAE at k=3 is 0.1763 with iva rows vs 0.1842 without on fold 0 (optimistic by 0.008), 0.1342 vs 0.1366 on fold 4; folds 1-3 move by <=0.0016 the other way. HEAD_FT/FULL_FT do not use the covariance, so the bias is one-sided toward the BLUP20 mechanism and toward the supports it picks.
findings.consequence: NNC[...]@BLUP20 inner scores (and the G14@BLUP20 inner score once it is added for the M* rule) are optimistic on the small folds, so nnc_mechanism can be chosen as BLUP20 over HEAD_FT/FULL_FT by a margin that does not exist; the registered arm NNC@SELECTED is then mis-specified. Outer test labels are not touched.
findings.fix: For select_on_inner, build the selection covariance from the three inner folds that exclude iva (e.g. inner_oof_curves with a skip set, or fold_covariance on the sub-fold whose train is itr with its own 3-way inner split), or hold the iva residual rows out of the pool; record 'n_rows_excluded' in the selection record and add a test that the covariance used in select_on_inner contains no residual row of fold.inner_validation_index.

findings.title: Outer NNC early-stops on an unmasked inner-validation set and trains on only 3/4 of the training fold
findings.detail: run_fold fits NNCArm(c2, val_index=fold.inner_validation_index).fit(ctx) (runner.py:149). NNCArm.fit sets tr_fit = setdiff1d(train, va) (nnc.py:123-126) and stops on the contrast loss of va (nnc.py:159-183) without applying cov.inner_mask. Under BP seed 104729 the stopping set shares publications with tr_fit on every fold: fold 0 4 shared publications / 9 of 65 tr_fit cells, fold 1 6 / 65 of 459, fold 2 5 / 51 of 437, fold 3 5 / 21 of 410, fold 4 2 / 4 of 369 (masked sizes would be 56, 394, 386, 389, 365). This violates IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md section 3.2 ('the design's mask re-applied inside the inner folds') for a selection step (the checkpoint). Separately, G14/FLAT/MEAN_CURVE/NN_TANIMOTO are fitted on all 76 training cells of fold 0 while NNC@ZERO sees 65, and the configuration was selected in select_on_inner with val_index=None (training-loss stopping, runner.py:108), i.e. under a different estimator than the one deployed. covs['NNC'] (runner.py:150-151) is likewise the residual covariance of a 2-seed, training-loss-stopped model, not of the deployed 8-seed iva-stopped ensemble.
findings.consequence: The stopping epoch is chosen on a laboratory-fingerprint-contaminated criterion, so NNC@ZERO/NNC@BLUP20 outer numbers under BP are not the pre-registered chemotype+publication-masked estimate (direction: checkpoints that fit publication-specific condition patterns are preferred, which under BP tends to hurt the outer score), and the Model 2 vs Model 1 comparison is confounded by a 25 % training-data handicap on the fold that holds out sc009.
findings.fix: In NNCArm.fit apply inner_mask(bench, ctx.design, tr_fit, va) before building the rows (pass design through ctx) and record n_fit/n_val/n_masked in fit_log; either refit the final ensemble on the full training fold with the epoch count chosen on the masked inner split, or give every arm the same tr_fit; use the same stopping rule in select_on_inner (carve a masked stopping set from itr) and build covs['NNC'] with that rule.

findings.title: The test suite does not guarantee plan section 4.4 claims 3-7 and 9, and two 'injection' tests inject nothing
findings.detail: Claim 3 (query labels unreachable, tested by NaN-masking queries and asserting identical predictions): test_adapters_see_only_support_values (lines 97-113) exercises blup/naive_line/ridge_line/rescale on a synthetic c0 only; the runner path (zero_curves, NNC head_ft_curves/full_ft_curves, unc_seq, select_on_inner) is never exercised with masked query labels. Claim 4 (supports never scored): no test reads an output table for support rows. Claim 5 (preprocessing fitted on training indices, 'fit-index logging'): nnc.py logs no fit indices and no test inspects self.pre. Claim 6 (selection records contain only inner scores): untested. Claim 7: only fold plans and random/uniform draws are hashed in the subprocess (lines 144-165); predictions are not. Claim 9 (every prediction row maps to a measured (cell, A, B)): untested. test_injected_held_out_residual_in_covariance_is_detected (test_leakage_injection.py:52-63) only records which indices inner_oof_curves visits; covariance_from_residuals (cov.py:102-111) accepts any rows, so a held-out residual inserted into the pool raises nothing, contrary to section 4.4 ('each must make the corresponding validator raise'). test_injected_unmasked_inner_training_is_detected (lines 66-74) re-tests inner_mask's output rather than injecting an unmasked set into a consumer. test_no_query_pair_is_arithmetically_determined (lines 80-87) covers WIDEST only; the joint-constraint issue above is not covered at all.
findings.consequence: A regression in any of: NNC preprocessing fit range, select_on_inner touching outer cells, support rows entering the table, or a held-out residual entering the covariance would pass the suite, while the plan and the pre-registration cite the suite as the executable guarantee.
findings.fix: Add tests that (a) run run_fold on one small BP fold with bench.Y query entries replaced by NaN after support reveal (monkey-patch DS.reveal to capture supports, then compare prediction columns), (b) assert the output table has no (cell, k, pair) row in sup.pairs and that every row's (A, B) are observed metals, (c) assert selection records reference only inner cells (spy on make_ctx), (d) tag CovRecord with the cell indices it was built from and make fold_covariance raise when any index is in fold.test_index (then inject one), (e) hash a prediction table in the subprocess test, (f) run the closure assertion for DOPT_Q/RANDOM with a real covariance on all cells.

findings.title: Outcome-bearing runs can bypass the pre-registration seal and truncate the cohort
findings.detail: --allow-unsealed (line 41, help text 'smoke only') is honoured for non-smoke runs: line 45 skips require_sealed_preregistration whenever the flag is set. --max-cells (line 38) is also accepted on non-smoke runs and truncates each fold's test set to its first N cells (runner.py:158-159) under any label. Nothing in the manifest marks such a run as invalid.
findings.consequence: A run labelled 'discovery' can be produced before the seal exists or on a partial cohort, and later be read as a result; the procedural guarantee stated in PRE_REGISTRATION.md (every outcome-bearing run checks the seal) does not hold.
findings.fix: Make --allow-unsealed and --max-cells imply smoke=True (force the label to start with 'smoke' and set cfg.smoke), and have manifest.Run record and refuse labels that collide with 'discovery'/'confirmation' when smoke is set.

findings.title: NNC@SELECTED silently becomes HEAD_FT with λ=1 wherever FULL_FT is not computed, and UNC_SEQ reuses a FULL_FT λ for the head refit
findings.detail: When sel['nnc_mechanism'] == 'FULL_FT', NNC@FULL_FT is computed only for policy DOPT_Q and k in {1, 3, 10} (lines 204-207); at every other (policy, k) line 208-209 substitutes preds['NNC@HEAD_FT'], which at that point was computed with λ=1.0 (line 203 uses the selected λ only when the mechanism is HEAD_FT). unc_seq (line 179) passes sel['nnc_lambda'] to head_ft_curves even when that λ was selected for FULL_FT.
findings.consequence: Exploratory NNC@SELECTED numbers at k in {2, 5, 8} and under RANDOM/WIDEST/UNIFORM/DOPT_CURVE/UNC_SEQ are a different arm from the registered one, so the 'R² vs k' curve for NNC@SELECTED mixes mechanisms, and the k-vs-0 exploratory contrasts for it are mislabelled; registered P1-P4 (DOPT_Q, k=3/10) are unaffected.
findings.fix: Either compute FULL_FT at every (policy, k) when it is the selected mechanism, or write NaN for NNC@SELECTED where it is not computed and record the substitution in meta; use the HEAD_FT λ grid winner (store it separately in rec) for unc_seq.

lenses.summary: Leakage/isolation review of gen20_kshot before sealing. Outer test labels and test publications do not reach any fitted object, covariance, support choice or prediction: BPG is a correct superset mask of BP with the inner split re-dealt by gen13's formula; inner_oof_curves iterates only the training fold with the design mask re-applied; zero-shot curves for test cells depend only on target-free LEAN features (209 columns, none log D-derived; repsd/nrep excluded); supports are revealed from support pairs only; the remaining regime excludes supports and per-pair-closed pairs; Setting B's support cell is asserted to be held out with the query and COPY is defined only on shared adjacent pairs. The 28 tests pass. Two blockers remain for the pre-registration itself: (1) the M* rule cannot execute because select_on_inner never records a G14@BLUP20 inner score, so decide_mstar always returns G14@BLUP20 (and --mstar allows a manual override at report time); (2) the no-closure rule stops per-pair closure only, while 25 % of adjacent-query degrees of freedom at C3/k=3 and 76 % at C10/k=10 are exactly fixed by the supports (e.g. support La/Pr fixes y(La/Ce)+y(Ce/Pr)), so the sealed text's 'algebraically independent' claim is false and P2/P3/P4 would be dominated by subtraction. Major defects: inner selection scores inner-validation cells with a covariance that pooled those cells' own residuals (up to 0.008 optimistic at k=3 on fold 0, biased toward BLUP20); the outer NNC early-stops on an unmasked inner-validation set sharing 2-6 publications with its training rows and trains on 3/4 of the fold; and the test suite does not establish plan section 4.4 claims 3-7/9 nor its covariance/unmasked-inner injection claims. Minor: --allow-unsealed and --max-cells work on non-smoke runs; NNC@SELECTED silently degrades to HEAD_FT(λ=1) where FULL_FT is not computed.

Software-defect lens on gen20_kshot before sealing. The core algebra is sound: gen20k.adapters.blup/blup_posterior reproduce gen15.fewshot exactly with R = noise*I, ridge_line reduces to OLS at lambda->0, naive_line/rescale are correct, inference._stats_from_sums (R2/MAE/RMSE), the tot - S leave-one-cluster jackknife and the multinomial draw matrix all match sklearn on a resampled toy table, the no-closure forest/bipartite rule is correct and reaches k_max, lighter-first orientation is consistent end to end, Setting B units/members/pairs (24/281/1397) match the plan, duplicates are removed on the frozen frame, the G14 covariance builds without fallback on every BP/B fold, and the 27 tests pass in 6 s. Six concrete defects remain, three of which touch the registered claims directly: (1) the pre-registered M* rule needs G14@BLUP20's inner k=3 score and select_on_inner never computes it; (2) the inner selection ladder uses the outer-fold covariance that already contains the scored inner-validation cells' own residual rows (11/73 on BP fold 0), and a clean inner covariance moves the inner k=3 BLUP20 MAE by up to 0.014; (3) inference.py hardcodes 95% percentile/BCa bounds while the pre-registration decides on 98.75% Bonferroni intervals; (4) NNC@SELECTED silently becomes HEAD_FT(lambda=1) wherever FULL_FT was not run, including k=0 of P2/P3 and every non-DOPT_Q policy; (5) FULL_FT fine-tunes with dropout live and an unseeded global torch RNG, so identical calls differ by 0.053 on a 0.42 correction; (6) Setting B's BLUP solves a rank-(n-1) 91x91 system with np.linalg.solve (cond 4e19) that happens to be benign today. Also minor: --allow-unsealed is not restricted to smoke labels, and the inner-selected NNC configuration is trained under a different stopping rule and training set than the deployed one. PRE_REGISTRATION.md is not yet sealed, so all of these can be fixed before any outcome-bearing run.

findings.title: M* cannot be chosen as pre-registered: select_on_inner never scores G14@BLUP20 on the inner ladder
findings.detail: PRE_REGISTRATION.md lines 68-69 fix the claim-carrying arm as 'NNC@SELECTED if its inner-selection score beats G14@BLUP20's inner score at k = 3 on a majority of (seed, fold) BP selections, otherwise G14@BLUP20', and says the choice is made before any outer score is read. select_on_inner (runner.py:80-129) fits a G14 arm on the inner training set at line 91 but uses it only for prior_coef(); the only entries written to rec['scores'] are RIDGE2@lam* and NNC[...]@zero/@BLUP20/@HEAD_FT/@FULL_FT. There is no G14@BLUP20 (or G14@zero) inner ladder, so the selection record saved in folds_<design>.json carries nothing the M* rule can be applied to. Reproduction: grep -n 'G14' gen20k/runner.py shows the G14 arm only at lines 91-92 and 140-152 (outer); no rec['scores']['G14@...'] key exists.
findings.consequence: After the discovery run, M* would have to be derived post hoc from a separate computation made after the outer tables exist, which the pre-registration (section 9, 'no arm ... chosen on an outer score') forbids in spirit and cannot audit; the claim-carrying arm for P1-P4 is therefore undefined at seal time. Whichever arm is picked later, the choice is unverifiable from the saved record.
findings.fix: In select_on_inner, after fitting g14 on ictx, add rec['scores']['G14@BLUP20'] = _ladder_mae(bench, iva, lambda ci, sup: AD.blup(g14.curves([ci])[0], cov_inner, sup, CV.noise_matrix(sup.pairs, s2)), cov_inner, s2) (and G14@zero with ks=(0,)), where cov_inner is the inner-training-only covariance from the next finding; record rec['nnc_beats_g14_inner_k3'] = bool(NNC selected k3 < G14 k3) so the majority rule is a one-line read of the selection records.

findings.title: Inner selection scores are computed with a covariance that contains the scored inner-validation cells' own residuals
findings.detail: select_on_inner receives ref_cov = CV.fold_covariance(bench, fold, G14) built in run_fold (line 140) from inner OOF residuals of every training cell, and passes ref_cov.cov both to the DOPT_Q support policy (via _ladder_mae) and to AD.blup for NNC[...]@BLUP20 at line 111-112. The inner-validation cells iva being scored are themselves training cells, so their centred residual rows are in that covariance. Measured on BP seed 104729: own rows in ref cov 11/73 (fold 0), 32/354, 39/340, 43/339, 10/257. Rebuilding the covariance from the masked inner-training cells only (CV.fold_covariance(bench, replace(fold, train_index=itr), ...)) changes the inner k=3 G14@BLUP20 MAE by -0.011, +0.0016, +0.0085, -0.0094, +0.0137 on folds 0-4, i.e. up to 0.014 in either direction, comparable to the 0.02 claim margin. The plan's test 6 ('selection records contain only inner scores') and section 3.2 ('inner selection ... never the outer test ... mask re-applied inside') are not met for the BLUP20 mechanism, and the same contaminated covariance is what the pre-registered M* rule would compare NNC@SELECTED against.
findings.consequence: The mechanism choice among BLUP20 / HEAD_FT / FULL_FT (and the M* comparison once the previous finding is fixed) is made on a BLUP20 score that is partly in-sample: on folds where the self-rows help it is biased toward selecting BLUP20, on others away from it, with swings of ~0.01 MAE on 10-43 cells. The inner-selection provenance guarantee the pre-registration advertises is false as implemented.
findings.fix: In select_on_inner build cov_inner = CV.fold_covariance(bench, replace(fold, train_index=itr), AR.as_fit_curves(facts['G14'])) (the inner_oof_curves re-deal then runs inside itr only) and use cov_inner.cov / cov_inner.noise_s2 for every _ladder_mae call and every AD.blup in the inner ladder; keep ref_cov for the outer loop. Add a test that monkeypatches CV.centred_residual during select_on_inner and asserts no inner-validation Y row is seen.

findings.title: inference.py hardcodes 95% intervals; the registered decision rule requires 98.75% Bonferroni intervals
findings.detail: PRE_REGISTRATION.md lines 92-93: 'Registered claims use Bonferroni over four: the intervals that decide are 98.75 %; 95 % intervals are descriptive.' pooled_contrasts computes lo, hi = np.quantile(fin, [0.025, 0.975]) at line 167, _bca iterates for q in (0.025, 0.975) at line 80, and pooled_levels uses 0.025/0.975 at lines 206-207. No alpha/level argument exists anywhere in the module (grep -n 'alpha' gen20k/inference.py returns nothing), so the code cannot produce the deciding interval, and PooledContrast has no field for a second level.
findings.consequence: If P1-P4 are decided with the only intervals the code can emit, a contrast whose 98.75% percentile or BCa interval covers 0 but whose 95% interval excludes it would be declared passing: the registered rule is applied at the wrong, more liberal, level and the direction of the error is always toward a false positive.
findings.fix: Add a level parameter to pooled_contrasts, _bca and pooled_levels (e.g. levels=(0.95, 0.9875)) and emit ci_low_95/ci_high_95/bca_*_95 and ci_low_9875/... columns, with the pre-registration naming which column decides; add a unit test that the 98.75% interval is at least as wide as the 95% one on the toy table.

findings.title: NNC@SELECTED silently carries HEAD_FT(lambda=1.0) wherever FULL_FT was not run, including k = 0 of P2/P3 and every non-DOPT_Q policy
findings.detail: FULL_FT is computed only when pol == cfg.full_ft_policy and k in cfg.full_ft_ks (line 204; DOPT_Q x {1, 3, 10}). Line 208-209 then maps NNC@SELECTED to preds.get('NNC@FULL_FT', preds['NNC@HEAD_FT']), and NNC@HEAD_FT at line 203 uses lambda = 1.0 whenever the selected mechanism is not HEAD_FT. Verified with run_fold on B seed 104729 fold 1 (3 cells, k_grid (0,1,3), select_on_inner stubbed to nnc_mechanism='FULL_FT'): NNC@FULL_FT is non-null only for (DOPT_Q, 1) and (DOPT_Q, 3); NNC@SELECTED equals NNC@HEAD_FT on all 16 other (policy, k) groups including (DOPT_Q, 0). A second mismatch sits in the same rows: FULL_FT averages only the first full_ft_members = 4 of the 8 outer members (line 55, 206-207) while HEAD_FT/BLUP20/ZERO average all 8 (measured: a 1-member vs 2-member mean differs by 0.0075 on a tiny net), so P2/P3 under a FULL_FT selection compare a 4-member fine-tuned ensemble at k = 3 with an 8-member zero-shot ensemble at k = 0.
findings.consequence: Every exploratory policy comparison for NNC@SELECTED (WIDEST, UNIFORM, RANDOM, DOPT_CURVE, UNC_SEQ) and every k not in {1, 3, 10} reports a prediction that is neither the selected mechanism nor its selected lambda, under the selected-arm column name; P2/P3's k = 0 baseline is a different estimator (8 members, no FT) from the k = 3 arm (4 members, FT), so part of delta(k) is ensemble-size and dropout-noise, not measurement value.
findings.fix: Write NaN for NNC@SELECTED (and NNC@FULL_FT) in rows where the selected mechanism was not actually computed, so downstream cohorts fail loudly rather than mislabel; compute FULL_FT at k = 0 too (it reduces to the member mean) and either use all 8 members for FULL_FT on the registered (DOPT_Q, k in {0,3,10}) rows or use the same 4-member subset for the k = 0 comparator; when the selected mechanism is HEAD_FT with lambda_sel, also record which lambda NNC@HEAD_FT used in a column.

findings.title: FULL_FT fine-tunes with dropout active and an unseeded global torch RNG, so the fine-tuned curve is not a function of its inputs
findings.detail: full_ft_curves calls net.train() at line 251 before the 30 Adam steps, so every forward pass inside the fine-tuning loop samples fresh dropout masks (p = 0.15 or 0.30) from torch's global generator, which is seeded only inside fit() (line 149) and advanced by every previous dropout draw. Reproduction on B seed 104729 fold 1, a 2-member 6-epoch arm, WIDEST k = 3 supports: two consecutive full_ft_curves(ci, sup, 1e-2, steps=30, members=2) calls with identical arguments differ by max |diff| = 0.053 while the correction itself is 0.42, i.e. ~12% of the signal is RNG noise. The head-only closed form (eval-mode features) and BLUP20 are deterministic, so the inner ladder in select_on_inner compares deterministic mechanisms against one whose score depends on how many FULL_FT calls preceded it in the same process; a partial re-run (different --max-cells, a single design, or the confirmation runner's different fold order) reproduces different NNC@FULL_FT and NNC@SELECTED values for the same cell.
findings.consequence: FULL_FT's inner-validation MAE is inflated by dropout variance, biasing the mechanism selection away from FULL_FT (or, when FULL_FT is selected, making NNC@SELECTED irreproducible); the plan's reproducibility test 7 (predictions reproduce in a subprocess) cannot hold for any row that contains FULL_FT.
findings.fix: Keep the copied net in eval mode during fine-tuning (LayerNorm is deterministic; dropout should be off for a 14-row adaptation), or if dropout during FT is intended, seed torch per call with torch.manual_seed(stable_seed('gen20', cell_id, member, k)) via a torch.random.fork_rng() context so the global stream is untouched; add a test that two identical full_ft_curves calls are equal.

findings.title: Setting B BLUP solves a rank-deficient system with np.linalg.solve; correct today by numerical accident
findings.detail: The support is every pair of the support cell (sv.pairs, the complete graph on its n metals, line 96) and AD.blup builds S = D (cov + s2 I) D^T of size n(n-1)/2 with rank n-1: for a 14-metal support cell S is 91 x 91 with rank 13 and condition number 3.8e19 (measured), and np.linalg.solve does not raise (LAPACK only raises on an exact zero pivot). The result coincided with the lstsq minimum-norm solution to 3e-13 on all 253 members with >= 3 support metals because the right-hand side r lies exactly in range(D) and the garbage null-space component is annihilated by cov D^T; that cancellation is not guaranteed under a different BLAS or once c0 carries float32 round-off.
findings.consequence: If the cancellation fails on another platform, every <arm>@BLUP20 column of the Setting B tables silently takes O(1e3+) values and the COPY-vs-BLUP20 comparison is garbage with no error raised; today the numbers are right but unreproducibly so.
findings.fix: Condition on a spanning tree of the support cell's metals (e.g. consecutive measured metals), which under R = s2 D D^T carries identical information to the complete graph and makes S full rank; or at minimum route this call through lstsq and assert np.linalg.matrix_rank(S) == len(pairs) in AD.blup before solve.

findings.title: --allow-unsealed is accepted with any label, not only smoke runs
findings.detail: The check is `if not a.smoke and not a.allow_unsealed: MF.require_sealed_preregistration()` (line 45-46). The help text at line 41 says 'smoke only', but nothing ties the flag to --smoke or to a label beginning with 'smoke', so `--label discovery --allow-unsealed` runs the full grid with 8-member ensembles against an unsealed pre-registration. The manifest records preregistration.sealed = False, which is auditable after the fact but does not prevent the run.
findings.consequence: An outcome-bearing table can be produced before the seal, contradicting the pre-registration header ('every outcome-bearing run checks it'); any such table would have to be discarded, and if it were not noticed the discovery numbers would predate the frozen protocol.
findings.fix: Reject the flag unless a.smoke is set (or a.label.startswith('smoke')), e.g. `if a.allow_unsealed and not a.smoke: ap.error('--allow-unsealed requires --smoke')`, and have RunConfig.smoke force max_cells and tiny ensembles so a non-smoke run can never be unsealed.

findings.title: Inner-selected NNC configuration is trained with a different stopping rule and training set than the deployed arm
findings.detail: select_on_inner fits each candidate with NNCArm(c2, val_index=None) (line 108): with no validation set, crit is the training loss (nnc.py line 173), which almost never stops early, so the inner candidates run to max_epochs = 300. The deployed arm (line 149) uses val_index = fold.inner_validation_index, stops on the inner-validation Huber contrast loss, and therefore trains on tr_fit = train minus inner-validation (nnc.py line 125: 57 of 76 cells on BP seed 104729 fold 0), with no publication mask between tr_fit and the stopping set under BP. The configuration ranked best on inner folds is thus a 300-epoch model on 100% of the inner-training cells, while the deployed model is an early-stopped model on 75% of the training fold whose stopping criterion can be fingerprint-driven.
findings.consequence: The selection record justifies a configuration that is not the estimator scored on the outer folds; NNC@SELECTED's outer MAE can be worse (or better) than the inner ranking implies for reasons unrelated to the configuration, and NNC is handicapped against G14 (which trains on the full fold) by 25% of the training cells, which the plan does not state.
findings.fix: Either train the inner candidates with the same validation-stopping rule on a further inner split carved from itr (so selection and deployment share the estimator), or deploy the selected configuration with the epoch count found on the inner fold and train on the full training fold; apply CV.inner_mask between tr_fit and val_index under BP/BPG; state the 75% training-fold fact in the plan.

findings.title: M* rule is not computable from the selection record and is never committed before outer scores exist
findings.detail: PRE_REGISTRATION.md §4 (line 67-69) says M* = NNC@SELECTED iff 'its inner-selection score beats G14@BLUP20's inner score at k = 3 on a majority of (seed, fold) BP selections'. Three things make this unexecutable as registered. (1) `select_on_inner` records only `RIDGE2@lam*` and `NNC[...]` keys (lines 93-120); the G14 arm fitted at line 91 is used only for `prior_coef()`, so no `G14@BLUP20` inner ladder score exists anywhere in `folds_BP.json` (grep confirms G14 appears only at lines 91, 141, 142, 152, 195). (2) NNC@SELECTED's inner score is `nanmean([k0, k3])` (line 122) while the rule names G14's score 'at k = 3'; k0 MAE is systematically larger than k3 MAE, so a literal reading pits an NNC average against a G14 k3-only number. (3) Nothing in `runner.run` or `manifest.Run` computes or records M*; the selection records and the outer prediction parquet are written by the same call into the same directory, so the 'before any outer score is read' guarantee is a promise, not a mechanism. The 25 votes are also wildly unequal: on BP seed 104729 fold 0 (sc009 held out) the inner-validation scoring set is 9 cells / 59 adjacent pairs; on seed 130363 fold 4 sc009 is the inner-validation fold itself (183 cells / 1136 pairs, inner-train = 93 non-diglycolamide cells), a different regime counted as one vote.
findings.consequence: The arm that carries P1-P4 is decided by code written after `pairs_BP.parquet` exists, with a comparator that has to be re-derived and an aggregator that is ambiguous. If NNC@SELECTED wins outer but loses the mis-specified inner comparison (k0/k3 mean vs k3), the registered claims are reported for G14@BLUP20 (or vice versa), and no reader can verify pre-commitment. Direction: a k0-inclusive NNC score vs a k3-only G14 score disfavours NNC; a vote dominated by 9-cell folds is close to a coin flip.
findings.fix: Add `G14@BLUP20` (and `G14@ZERO`) to `rec['scores']` via the same `_ladder_mae(bench, iva, ..., ks=(0,3))` call; state in §4 that both sides use the same aggregator (k3 only, or the (k0,k3) mean) and a pair-weighted or per-seed-pooled vote with a tie rule; have `runner.run` compute M* from the selection records and write it to `run_summary.json` and the manifest before any parquet is written, or split inner selection into a separate sealed stage that runs first.

findings.title: The deciding 98.75 % intervals cannot be produced, and the percentile∧BCa conjunction is not conservative on this cluster profile
findings.detail: PRE_REGISTRATION.md §6 (lines 90-93): 'Registered claims use Bonferroni over four: the intervals that decide are 98.75 %'. `pooled_contrasts` hard-codes `np.quantile(fin, [0.025, 0.975])` (line 167) and `_bca` hard-codes `(0.025, 0.975)` (line 80); there is no alpha parameter, and `mde_80 = 2.80*se` (line 130) is the 95 % MDE, not the 98.75 % one (3.34*se). The rule also keeps 'percentile p < 0.05' and 'wild-cluster-t p < 0.05' beside the 98.75 % intervals, i.e. unadjusted thresholds next to an adjusted interval. Null simulation of `pooled_contrasts` on the real C3 per-chemotype pair counts (39 clusters, 1008/1980 pairs in sc009; 300 sims × 2000 draws; scratch script null_sim2.py): rejection of 'percentile ∧ BCa ∧ p<0.05' at nominal 5 % = 4.0 / 9.3 / 5.7 / 9.7 % for cluster-effect sd 0 / 0.03 / 0.05 / 0.05 (row sd 0.30); BCa alone = 5 / 17 / 13 / 20 %, percentile alone = 6 / 12 / 6 / 10 %. With one dominant cluster BCa is less conservative than percentile, so requiring both ≈ percentile alone.
findings.consequence: Per registered MAE/R² claim the false-positive rate is ~1.2-2× nominal and the family-wise rate over four claims is ~0.2-0.3 if the code is used as it stands; the reported interval for every registered contrast is a 95 % interval labelled as deciding. A true-null P1 or P4 ('model beats the line') passes too often; P3 (R²) has no wild-cluster-t backstop at all.
findings.fix: Add `alpha` to `pooled_contrasts`/`pooled_levels`/`_bca` and run the registered contrasts at alpha = 0.0125 (p thresholds 0.0125 for percentile and WCR, mde at 3.34*se); for the three MAE claims make the calibrated statistic the decider: run `gen13sep.wildcluster.wild_cluster_t` (CR2) on the per-row paired |e_ref|-|e_cand| clustered by chemotype (the pooled estimand), not only on per-extractant deltas; define a NaN BCa bound as a failed criterion; drop the BCa conjunction from the rule or report the simulated size beside it.

findings.title: Effective number of chemotypes on the registered rows is 3.6, not 11.7, and the rule mixes a pooled effect size with a macro-estimand p-value
findings.detail: Counted on the bench (scratch cohort_stats.py): strict-adjacent query pairs in C3: 1980, sc009 = 1008 (50.9 %), Kish effective chemotypes 3.6 (C0 3.3, C5 4.1, C10 4.5 with sc009 43.7 %); Kish effective extractants 12.3. The 'Kish 11.7' of AUDIT.md:161 / IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:204 is the cell-level figure for all 521 cells, not the pair-weighted figure for the rows `pooled_contrasts` resamples. P(sc009 absent from a bootstrap draw) = (38/39)^39 = 0.36, so every bootstrap distribution is a two-component mixture and `loco_all_positive` is decided essentially by the single sc009-out value. §5/§7 never say whether the registered 'MAE' is pooled or extractant-macro (`pooled_contrasts` can only do pooled; `unit_mae_contrast` does extractant-macro), and §6 now requires the pooled point ≥ 0.02 and pooled intervals but a wild-cluster-t p computed on per-extractant deltas — two estimands that the programme has already seen rank arms in opposite orders (gen2 macro-vs-micro trap). C3 is also easier than the excluded cells: FLAT MAE 0.163 on C3 vs 0.228 on the 134 pairs of cells with k_max < 3 (label-free selection, but the k=0 levels are not the full-cohort levels).
findings.consequence: The headline ΔMAE for P1/P2/P4 and its interval are ~51 % one chemotype: a diglycolamide-only gain passes as 'chemically unseen extractants', while a gain spread over the other 38 chemotypes can fail the pooled 0.02 threshold; the point estimate reported is not the quantity the calibrated p tests. Direction: pooled numbers track sc009; macro numbers track the small chemotypes.
findings.fix: Name the estimand in §7 explicitly. Register chemotype-macro (or extractant-macro, Kish 12.3) MAE as the deciding metric with the wild-cluster-t on the matching per-unit deltas, and require the sc009-excluded pooled contrast to meet the 0.02 margin (not just the LOCO sign); print the pair-weighted Kish per cohort (3.6 / 4.1 / 4.5) in §6 in place of 11.7; print FLAT and n per cohort in every table and state that C3 excludes the 2-4-metal cells.

findings.title: Inner-selection covariance is estimated partly from the inner-validation cells it then scores
findings.detail: `inner_oof_curves` pools OOF residuals from all four inner folds of the training fold (loop at line 74). `run_fold` builds `ref = covs['G14']` from it (runner.py:140-142) and passes it to `select_on_inner` (runner.py:144), whose `_ladder_mae` uses `ref_cov.cov` both for the DOPT_Q supports (line 71) and for the BLUP20 inner scores (line 112) on `fold.inner_validation_index` — which is the first of those same four inner folds. Measured overlap (scratch inner_sel.py, BP): inner-validation cells supply 10/73, 32/354, 32/340, 41/339, 10/257 residual rows on seed 104729 folds 0-4 and 269/355 = 76 % on seed 130363 fold 4. The outer covariance used on the test cells is clean (test cells never enter the pool; tests confirm).
findings.consequence: BLUP20 inner scores are in-sample-optimistic relative to HEAD_FT/FULL_FT, which use no covariance, so `nnc_mechanism` is tilted toward BLUP20 and the (to-be-added) G14@BLUP20 comparator in the M* vote is inflated by the same amount; on the 76 %-overlap fold the inner BLUP is close to a leave-nothing-out fit. Outer numbers are not affected, but the registered arm and its mechanism are chosen on a biased criterion. Direction: inner BLUP20 MAE too low; NNC HEAD_FT/FULL_FT under-selected.
findings.fix: Inside `select_on_inner` build the selection covariance from the other three inner folds only (call `inner_oof_curves` on `itr` with its own 4-way deal, or drop `iva` rows from the pool), so the covariance that scores `iva` has never seen `iva`; record the overlap count in the selection record.

findings.title: The analysis path from the long table to the four claims does not exist, so the seal freezes predictions but not decisions
findings.detail: No `report.py`/`g20_report.py` exists (plan §4.1 lists them). `pooled_contrasts` compares two columns of one table, but P2/P3 contrast k = 3 rows against k = 0 rows of the same column and P1/P4 need the filter (design BP, policy DOPT_Q, draw 0, regime Q, k_max ≥ 3 or ≥ 10); the pivot and the cohort filter are unwritten. `benjamini_hochberg` is never called and the exploratory family is not enumerated. RANDOM writes five identical k = 0 rows per cell (lines 173-175 then 183-186 for every draw) and §3 says nothing about how the five draws are aggregated when RANDOM is compared with the one-draw policies on 'identical Q'.
findings.consequence: Each of these is a degree of freedom exercised with the outer table on disk. Concrete example: averaging the five RANDOM draws' predictions before scoring gives the MAE of an ensemble-mean prediction and flatters RANDOM against DOPT_Q (direction: policy gap understated); counting the BH family after the fact changes which exploratory p-values survive (direction: a smaller family makes more of them 'significant'); five stacked k = 0 rows inflate n in any pooled table that is not de-duplicated.
findings.fix: Write and seal `g20_report.py` before the discovery run: cohort filters, the k-pivot on (seed, cell_id, A, B), M* from the selection record, alpha = 0.0125, an enumerated exploratory family (policies × k × arm-pairs × designs × cohorts, counted in the script), draw aggregation = mean of per-draw MAE with draw 0 used for 'identical Q' comparisons, and a test that runs it end-to-end on a smoke table.

findings.title: NNC@SELECTED and NNC@HEAD_FT silently switch to an unselected mechanism or λ outside DOPT_Q k ∈ {1, 3, 10}
findings.detail: When `sel['nnc_mechanism'] == 'FULL_FT'`, `NNC@SELECTED` falls back to `preds['NNC@HEAD_FT']` (line 209) for every policy other than DOPT_Q and for k ∈ {2, 5, 8}; that HEAD_FT column is computed with λ = 1.0 whenever the selected mechanism is not HEAD_FT (line 203), although §4 says HEAD_FT's penalty is inner-chosen. P1-P4 (DOPT_Q, k = 3/10) are unaffected.
findings.consequence: The exploratory policy ladders and the 'Model 2 vs Model 1 at each k' table attribute to NNC@SELECTED a mechanism that was not selected, so the k = 2/5/8 points of the NNC curve are not comparable to k = 1/3/10 and the HEAD_FT column carries an arbitrary λ. Direction: unpredictable per fold; the NNC ladder looks non-monotone for reasons unrelated to k.
findings.fix: Either compute FULL_FT wherever it is the selected mechanism, or write NaN for NNC@SELECTED where its mechanism is unavailable; record the λ actually used per column in the fold metadata.

findings.title: Inner selection trains NNC in a different regime than the deployed arm, and the deployed stopping set is unmasked
findings.detail: `select_on_inner` fits `NNCArm(c2, val_index=None)` (line 108), which stops on the training loss (nnc.py:172-183), i.e. effectively runs to `max_epochs = 300`; the outer arm (line 149) early-stops on `fold.inner_validation_index` and trains on `tr_fit = setdiff(train, va)` (nnc.py:125-126) with no `inner_mask` between `tr_fit` and `va`, so the stopping criterion sees the 94 %-identifiable publication fingerprint.
findings.consequence: Configuration, mechanism, λ and the NNC side of the M* vote are chosen on over-trained models the outer never deploys (direction: NNC inner scores pessimistic, G14 favoured as M*); the deployed NNC sees 25 % fewer training cells than G14 and a stopping epoch tuned on a leaky criterion (direction: exploratory Model 2 vs Model 1 contrasts biased against NNC).
findings.fix: In `select_on_inner`, carve a masked stopping set inside `itr` so the inner models use the same stopping rule as the outer ones; in the outer fit apply `inner_mask` to `tr_fit` against `va`, or refit on the full training fold for the chosen epoch count.

findings.title: metrics.pooled reports n_rows from y while MAE/R² silently drop rows with NaN predictions
findings.detail: `n_rows = isfinite(y).sum()` (line 58) but `mae`/`rmse`/`r2` use `ok = isfinite(y) & isfinite(p)`. `NNC@FULL_FT` is NaN outside DOPT_Q k ∈ {1, 3, 10}, so on any table that is not pre-filtered its MAE and R² are computed on a different row set than the other arms under the same printed n. (`pooled_contrasts` behaves differently: a NaN prediction poisons the cluster sums at inference.py:41-45 and the whole contrast becomes NaN, which is at least visible.)
findings.consequence: A metrics table can show FULL_FT scored only on its DOPT_Q rows beside arms scored on all rows, with identical n_rows, violating the identical-population contract (direction: FULL_FT compared on an easier or harder subset without any flag).
findings.fix: Compute n_rows from the ok mask, return it beside the y count, and raise when two arms in one table differ in their ok-row sets.

lenses.summary: The prediction side of gen20_kshot is leakage-clean as far as I can verify (28 tests pass; query/support isolation, closure rule, PSD inner-OOF covariance on the outer folds, training-only preprocessing and BP masks all hold), but the decision layer is not frozen and should not be sealed as written. Blockers: (1) the M* rule cannot be evaluated from the selection record (no G14@BLUP20 inner score is computed; NNC's score is a (k0,k3) mean while the rule names k3; nothing records M* before the outer parquet exists; votes range from 9 to 183 cells); (2) the registered 98.75 % Bonferroni intervals cannot be produced by inference.py (0.025/0.975 hard-coded at lines 80 and 167), and a null simulation on the real C3 cluster sizes shows the percentile∧BCa∧p rule rejecting 4-10 % at nominal 5 % with BCa alone at 13-20 % (BCa is the anti-conservative bound when one cluster holds half the rows). Major: the registered rows have 3.6 Kish-effective chemotypes (sc009 = 51 % of C3 pairs), not the 11.7 quoted, and §6/§7 mix a pooled effect size with a per-extractant wild-cluster-t p; the inner-selection covariance is built from residuals that include the inner-validation cells it scores (14-76 % overlap per fold), tilting mechanism choice toward BLUP20; and the entire analysis path (k-pivot, cohort filters, RANDOM-draw aggregation, BH family) is unwritten. Minor: NNC@SELECTED silently falls back to an unselected mechanism/λ outside DOPT_Q k∈{1,3,10}; inner NNC models are trained without early stopping while the deployed arm early-stops on an unmasked quarter of the training fold; metrics.pooled's n_rows does not reflect NaN-prediction drops. Setting B's duplicate filter was checked and works (24 units, no duplicate pair survives in one unit).

findings.title: The pre-registered M* rule cannot be executed: no inner G14@BLUP20 score is ever computed, and the NNC inner key aggregates k=0 and k=3 while the rule says k=3
findings.detail: PRE_REGISTRATION.md:67-69 says the arm carrying P1-P4 is `NNC@SELECTED` if its inner-selection score beats `G14@BLUP20`'s inner score at k = 3 on a majority of BP (seed, fold) selections, otherwise `G14@BLUP20`. `select_on_inner` (runner.py:80-129) writes `rec['scores']` with keys `RIDGE2@lam*`, `NNC[cfg]@zero`, `NNC[cfg]@BLUP20`, `NNC[cfg]@HEAD_FT@lam*`, `NNC[cfg]@FULL_FT@lam*` and nothing else; `grep -n 'G14@BLUP20' runner.py scripts/g20_discovery.py` returns nothing. The `g14` arm fitted at line 91 is used only for `prior_coef()`. The NNC winner at line 121-122 is chosen by `nanmean([cands[k][0], cands[k][3]])` (mean of the k=0 and k=3 ladders), not the k=3 score the rule names, so even the NNC side of the comparison is not the registered quantity.
findings.consequence: After the discovery run there is no registered number to compare against: M* would have to be chosen post hoc (the pre-registration's own §9 forbids choosing an arm on an outer score) or by an unregistered inner score computed later. P1-P4 are therefore undefined at seal time; whichever way M* is then picked, the registered MAE contrasts (and the confirmation run, which must reuse 'the same inner-selection procedure') cannot be audited against the sealed text.
findings.fix: In `select_on_inner`, add `rec['scores']['G14@BLUP20'] = _ladder_mae(bench, iva, lambda ci, sup: AD.blup(g14.curves([ci])[0], ref_cov.cov, sup, CV.noise_matrix(sup.pairs, s2)), ref_cov.cov, s2)` and record `rec['nnc_beats_g14_at_k3'] = cands[key][3] < rec['scores']['G14@BLUP20'][3]`; make the NNC key and the registered rule use the same aggregation (k=3 only, or write 'mean of k=0 and k=3' into §4); add a test asserting the selection record carries the comparison; have the report derive M* from the majority of these flags, never from pairs_*.parquet.

findings.title: The no-closure rule treats a separation factor as the atomic measurement; a laboratory reads log D per metal, so 30-33 % of C3 queries at k=3 and 77-100 % of C10 queries at k=10 are pairs whose both metals the laboratory has already measured
findings.detail: Every value in the bundle is a per-metal log D; log SF is derived. A support pair (a,b) therefore costs two D readings, and any two metals that both carry a reading in the same cell have a known SF regardless of which forest edges were 'measured'. `legal_candidates` (design.py:129-142) only forbids algebraic closure through the forest, not experimental closure through the read metals. Counted on the bench with the G14 inner-OOF covariance of BP seed 104729 fold 1: on the C3 cohort (275 cells, 1 980 adjacent queries) at k=3 the fraction of query pairs with BOTH metals already read is DOPT_Q 654/1980 = 33.0 % (in every one of the 275 cells), WIDEST 29.9 %, RANDOM 21.9 %, UNIFORM 16.2 %. On C10 (114 cells, 1 297 queries) at k=10: DOPT_Q 77.3 % (12.0 of >=12 metals read), WIDEST 76.7 %, RANDOM 80.3 %, UNIFORM 100 % (13.7 metals read). Example cell 7ae1cf22d55d9cc1, WIDEST k=3 = La/Lu, La/Tm, Ce/Yb: the laboratory has D for La, Ce, Tm, Yb, Lu and already knows the 'queries' La/Ce, Tm/Yb, Yb/Lu. At k = k_max = n-2 the two trees cover every metal, so every query is known; 5-metal cells (21 of C3) reach that at k=3. Policies are also compared at equal k but unequal cost: at k=3 on >=12-metal cells UNIFORM and DOPT_Q read 6.0 metals, WIDEST 5.0; 'UNIFORM' always adds two unread metals as a short pair in the largest gap (La/Lu, Sm/Gd, Pr/Ho), i.e. it is not farthest-point coverage and is the most expensive policy per pair.
findings.consequence: P2/P3 (M* k=3 vs k=0 on C3) and P4 (k=10 on C10) are scored on pairs no laboratory would need predicted; those are exactly the pairs where the BLUP interpolates between two measured components, so excluding them raises every k-shot MAE and lowers every ΔR² (k-shot gains overstated, P2/P3 'expected positive' is partly a design artefact). P4 describes an experiment that cannot occur: a laboratory with D for 12 of 14 metals has every adjacent SF, so any P4 'gain over LINE' is uninterpretable in either direction. The secondary question 'which policy is worth the most' compares unequal numbers of D readings.
findings.fix: Model the support as a metal subset S (k = |S| D readings; the support list is any spanning tree of S, which carries identical information) and the query as the adjacent pairs with at least one metal outside S; the no-closure rule then reduces to 'no query inside S'. Minimum change before sealing: add a boolean `lab_known` (both endpoints in {m for e in supports for m in e}) to every query row in `run_fold`, define C3/C5/C10 and P1-P4 on `lab_known == False` rows, print the number of distinct metals read beside k in every policy table, and drop or relabel P4 (k=10 leaves at most the queries touching the unread metals).

findings.title: The registered noise constant s² is the squared median of a bimodal replicate-sd distribution contaminated by decade-level double entries: it implies an SF noise sd (0.43) larger than the target's total sd (0.23), so every BLUP arm keeps 78 % of its prior at each support
findings.detail: `training_noise_s2` (cov.py:93-100) takes the median `repsd__` over training cells and squares it; the runner uses `R = s2*DDᵀ` (runner.py:188) and `2*s2` for DOPT (runner.py:181). On the bench: 216 of 3 359 observed (cell, metal) readings are replicated; repsd quantiles 10/25/50/75/90/max = 0.007/0.061/0.302/0.679/1.066/1.613; 36 % exceed 0.5 and 12 % exceed 1.0 log unit (a factor of 10 in D is not replicate scatter). Among the 24 nrep=2 readings whose two values differ by >= 0.95 decades, 12 are within 0.05 of an integer number of decades (0.96-1.03, 1.94-1.98): the exponent-corruption signature recorded for DMDPhPDA; the extractants carrying repsd > 1 are DGAs (TODGA, TDDGA, T2EHDGA ...). Registered s = 0.302 gives s² = 0.0914 (0.0924 on BP seed 104729 fold 1) and Var(log SF) = 2s² = 0.183, sd 0.43, against the observed strict-adjacent y variance 0.0535 (sd 0.231, n = 2 114): a genuine replicate floor cannot exceed the total variance 3.4-fold. The median of readings <= 0.5 is 0.106 (2s² = 0.022). BLUP weight on a support of signal variance 0.0535: 0.22 with the registered s², 0.73 with 0.106, 0.37 with gen15's 0.09. Chemistry: within one experiment the phase-ratio and calibration errors of D(A) and D(B) cancel in SF, so SF noise is below 2·Var(D), not equal to it. The 'gen15' kind (cov.py:132-134) puts 2s² = 0.185 on the diagonal, not gen15's NOISE_VAR 0.09, so `G14@BLUP_INDEP` is not the replication arm the plan (lines 331-332) and AUDIT B.3 describe; and the plan's own risk 1 (line 189) quotes 'a replicate floor of ~0.21 on one log SF', which matches neither 0.302·√2 nor the registered R. No cell's nrep enters R, so a mean of 8 replicates is given the same noise as a single reading.
findings.consequence: Every @BLUP20/@BLUP_INDEP arm and RIDGE2 (R⁻¹-weighted) under-use the supports while LINE uses them fully: P1 and P4 are biased toward 'no gain over the line' and P2/P3 downward by a constant that is a data-corruption artefact; the DOPT_CURVE/DOPT_Q information gains are computed under the same inflated noise and flatten toward WIDEST-like choices; the gen15 replication numbers (0.1700 at D-optimal k=3) will not reproduce under the mislabelled 'gen15' R.
findings.fix: Estimate s² robustly from the replicate readings after removing integer-decade double entries (e.g. median of repsd <= 0.5, or a MAD-based scale), or better from replicate SFs directly where both metals of a pair are replicated in a cell; register a sanity assertion `2*s2 < Var(y_adjacent)` per fold; divide the per-reading variance by nrep where a reading is a replicate mean; let `kind='gen15'` use the literal 0.09; state in §3.4 that SF errors are smaller than D errors and treat s² as an upper bound with a lower-s² sensitivity arm.

findings.title: The gen13-adjacency secondary (Nd–Sm) promised 'alongside for continuity' is never run; Nd/Sm, the operationally adjacent pair of every Pm-free feed, is only ever a floating remaining-regime row or a support
findings.detail: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:36 and :240 and data.py:10-11 commit to reporting 'adjacent + Nd–Sm' beside the strict set; `make_design` (design.py:45-54) accepts `query_name='adjacent_gen13'` but `run_fold` only ever calls `DS.make_design(cv)` with the default, and `grep adjacent_gen13 gen20k scripts` finds no caller. Nd–Sm (dZ = 2) is a legal support: the deterministic policies take it in 0-1 of 114 C10 cells, RANDOM in 3/4/6/9/16 of 114 cells at k = 1/2/3/5/10. Nd/Sm therefore reaches the long table only as a regime 'R' row (under B and BP, three sequences only) and only when it was not chosen as a support. PRE_REGISTRATION.md §2 is silent on the secondary.
findings.consequence: The continuity number against gen15's gen13-adjacent MAE 0.139 (AUDIT A.2) cannot be produced on a fixed population; any post-hoc reconstruction from R rows changes population with k and policy and drops the cells where Nd–Sm was measured, biasing the Nd/Sm MAE toward the cells where RANDOM happened not to pick it. The report would be unable to say anything about the one pair (Nd/Sm) a magnet-recycling or Pm-free separation actually needs.
findings.fix: Either run a second, labelled query set `adjacent_gen13` through `run_fold` under BP (its own forest, k_max and cohorts; Nd–Sm then leaves the candidate set) and write it to its own parquet, or strike the 'reported alongside' promise from the plan and state in PRE_REGISTRATION.md §2 that Nd/Sm is not evaluated.

findings.title: §1.5/§4.3 understate what was changed from the reference: full-batch training, a different stopping criterion, the outer NNC trained on fewer cells than G14 (with an unmasked validation set), and selection run with a different stopping rule than deployment; the arm is the reference's control, not its model
findings.detail: Reference `automl/topo/train.py` (clone at /Users/lilshadix/PycharmProjects/lanthanidestrain): whole-composition-block mini-batches of `batch_rows=64` (lines 940-975), AdamW with `CosineAnnealingLR` (680), 60 epochs, patience 6, early stopping on inner MSE or adjacent R² (1176-1200), ensembles of 16. gen20 `NNCArm.fit` (nnc.py:148-188) takes ONE full-batch step per epoch (<= 300 steps vs ~2 200 reference steps on the 2 370-row inner-train of BP seed 104729 fold 1), no schedule, and stops on the adjacent-weighted Huber contrast loss; §4.3 lists only the R²→MAE change, which is itself no longer what the code does. The head does train (training crit 0.25 → 0.044 over 300 steps; outer-style fits stop at 147-158 epochs), so this is a fidelity-of-claim gap, not a convergence failure. Undocumented handicaps against Model 1: `tr_fit = np.setdiff1d(tr, va)` (nnc.py:125) removes the inner-validation cells from the outer NNC's training set (459 of 491 cells on fold 1; ~57 of 76 on the sc009 fold) while G14 uses all; the BP mask is not re-applied between `tr_fit` and `va`, so the stopping criterion is evaluated with publication leakage; `select_on_inner` fits every candidate with `val_index=None` (runner.py:101-108: training-loss stopping, effectively 300 epochs) while the deployed arm (runner.py:149) stops on inner-validation loss, so the configuration is chosen for a procedure that is not the one deployed. PRE_REGISTRATION.md:28 calls Model 2 'the reference-derived neural contrast model'; it is the reference's zero-width `TabularNet` CONTROL, for which the reference measured the contrast objective at +0.030 adjacent R² against +0.186 for its simplicial encoder, with its headline from an anchored CatBoost (plan lines 130-134).

findings.fix: Add rows to §4.3 for batching/schedule/step budget, the stopping criterion, the training-set difference and the selection/deployment stopping mismatch; train the outer NNC on all training cells with the epoch count fixed from the inner fits (or carve a masked validation set with `inner_mask` applied); use the same stopping rule in `select_on_inner` and `run_fold`; rename the arm in PRE_REGISTRATION.md to 'reference tabular control (TabularNet + contrast objective)' and say that the reference's encoder and anchored CatBoost are not tested.

findings.title: Inner selection on the sc009 fold rests on 9-27 inner-validation cells, and the BLUP20 candidates are scored with a covariance whose residual pool contains those very cells' residual curves
findings.detail: `select_on_inner` uses only the stored first inner fold: on the folds holding out sc009 the masked inner-train has 48-56 cells and the inner-validation set 11-30 cells, of which 9/10/20/14/27 (seeds 104729/130363/155921/196613/262147) have k_max >= 3 and enter `_ladder_mae` (59-277 adjacent pairs). `ref_cov` passed in is `fold_covariance` over the whole training fold, whose `inner_oof_curves` (cov.py:68-83) re-deals the same inner split with `inner_seed(fold.seed, fold.fold)`, so the inner-validation cells' own centred residuals are 1/4 of the pooled covariance used to score `NNC[...]@BLUP20` (runner.py:108-112) on those same cells; `@HEAD_FT` and `@FULL_FT` get no such advantage.

findings.title: The radius basis is Shannon's effective ionic radii, not 'crystal radii' as the frozen docstring the plan cites says
findings.detail: `SHANNON_RADIUS_CN8` (La 1.160 ... Lu 0.977 Å) and `SHANNON_RADIUS_CN9` (La 1.216 ... Lu 1.032 Å) are Shannon 1976 effective ionic radii; Shannon's crystal radii are 0.14 Å larger (La³⁺ CN8 1.30 Å). The plan (§1.4, AUDIT B.4 'standardised Shannon CN8 radius') inherits the label. Because `physics_basis` standardises each vector, the constant offset cancels exactly and no number changes; aqueous Ln³⁺ hydration numbers run 9 (La-Nd) to 8 (Tb-Lu), so CN8 alone is a convention, but the standardised CN8 and CN9 vectors are nearly collinear.
findings.consequence: None numerically; a reader checking the radii against Shannon's tables will find the 'crystal' values do not match and may suspect the basis.
findings.fix: Say 'Shannon effective ionic radii (CN 8; CN 9 kept as an alternative)' in the plan's §1.4 and leave the frozen file alone.

lenses.summary: Tests pass (28) and the leakage machinery is sound; the defects are in what the design claims to measure. Three must be fixed before sealing. (1) The pre-registered M* rule has no implementation: `select_on_inner` never scores G14@BLUP20 on the inner fold and aggregates the NNC key over k=0 and k=3 while the rule says k=3, so P1-P4 cannot be assigned an arm by the registered procedure. (2) The no-closure rule models a separation factor as the atomic measurement, but the bundle is per-metal log D: at k=3 on C3, 30-33 % of the scored 'queries' (DOPT_Q 654/1980, in every cell) are pairs whose both metals the laboratory has already read, and at k=10 on C10 it is 77-100 % (UNIFORM reads 13.7 of 14 metals); P4 describes an experiment that cannot occur and P2/P3's expected positive sign is partly a design artefact; policies are compared at equal k but unequal D-reading cost. (3) The registered noise constant squares the median of a bimodal replicate-sd distribution carrying integer-decade double entries (12 % of 'replicates' differ by more than a decade; 12 of 24 large nrep=2 differences are within 0.05 of a whole decade), giving an SF noise sd 0.43 against a target sd 0.23 and a BLUP support weight of 0.22 instead of ~0.73; every BLUP arm is handicapped against LINE, the DOPT policies use the same inflated noise, and the 'gen15' R is 0.185 not 0.09, so the replication arm is mislabelled. Major: the promised Nd–Sm continuity secondary is never run (Nd/Sm, the operationally adjacent pair in any Pm-free feed, exists only as floating remaining-regime rows), and §4.3 omits four deviations from the reference (full-batch steps, a different stopping criterion, the outer NNC trained on fewer cells than G14 with an unmasked validation set, selection under a different stopping rule than deployment) while the pre-registration names the reference's weakest control 'the reference-derived model'. Minor: 'chemically unseen' is DGA-to-DGA on the fold carrying 54 % of adjacent pairs (the family is 426/521 cells, 17 DGA cells remain in that fold's 76-cell training set); inner selection on that fold rests on ~9 cells and scores BLUP20 with a covariance containing those cells' residuals; the radii are Shannon effective ionic radii, not 'crystal radii' (numerically irrelevant). Checked and found sound: strict adjacency and the reference's own exclusion of Nd/Sm (its docstring says so), lighter-first orientation, promethium handling, the sc009/TODGA counts, the no-3D-port justification, the expected-results section as a statement of direction, and Setting B's singular 91-pair BLUP system (consistent; equals the spanning-tree BLUP to machine precision).

verdicts.label: verify:leakage:Outcome-bearing runs can bypas

Code facts hold: generations/gen20_kshot/scripts/g20_discovery.py:45 gates MF.require_sealed_preregistration() on `not a.smoke and not a.allow_unsealed`, so `--label discovery --allow-unsealed` without `--smoke` skips the seal check and runs with cfg.smoke=False (replicated the parser read-only: seal-check-runs=False for that combination); `--max-cells N` on a non-smoke run flows via g20_discovery.py:52 into RunConfig.max_cells (runner.py:76, comment 'smoke runs only' is not enforced) and runner.py:158-159 truncates every fold's test set to its first N cells of fold.test_index. verdicts.label: verify:leakage:Inner selection scores inner-v
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED. Reproduced read-only (G14 as the zero curve, BP, all 5 registered seeds). Magnitude: seed 104729 matches the claim exactly (iva share 13.7/9.0/9.4/12.1/3.9 %; k=3 inner BLUP20 MAE with-minus-without iva rows -0.0079/+0.0015/+0.0010/+0.0008/-0.0024). Across all 25 BP (seed, fold) selections the mean difference is -0.0112, 20/25 folds optimistic, extremes -0.068 (seed 155921 fold 1: 0.121 vs 0.189), -0.052 (262147 f2), -0.028, -0.025, -0.024; on 4 folds the stored first inner fold holds the largest chemotype so iva is 74-77 % of the pool (e.g. 269/355, 255/344), i.e. the 'selection covariance' is essentially the scored chemotype's own residual covariance. DOPT_Q k=3 support sequences also change (3/9, 20/31, 6/16, 25/26, 0/9 cells on seed 104729). Consequence if unfixed: the per-fold nnc_mechanism choice (runner.py:121-126, driven by the k=3 term) can go to BLUP20 over HEAD_FT/FULL_FT on a margin of ~0.01 (up to 0.07) that an honest inner score does not show, and the registered M* majority rule (PRE_REGISTRATION §4: NNC@SELECTED vs G14@BLUP20 inner score at k=3, which select_on_inner does not yet compute) is tilted toward G14@BLUP20 whenever NNC selects a fine-tuning mechanism; the recorded inner 'scores' for every *@BLUP20 key are in-sample numbers. Not a blocker: outer test labels and the outer covariance are untouched, so every registered outer estimate stays honest for whichever arm is picked; it mis-specifies the registered arm choice and records wrong selection numbers, hence major. No test covers it (tests/ has no select_on_inner assertion). Fix as proposed: pool only the three inner folds whose validation part is not iva (skip set in inner_oof_curves or a hold-out of iva residual rows) for the covariance passed to select_on_inner, record n_rows_excluded, and add a test that no residual row of fold.inner_validation_index enters the selection covariance.

The claim's own "at minimum" fix is therefore already implemented. The rank-deficiency structure it describes is real — I confirmed on the loaded bench that setting_b.units() yields 24 units / 281 members, 253 with >= 3 support metals, and the largest support is the 91-pair complete graph with S of rank 13 (cond ~3e19) — but lstsq is the correct and platform-robust solver here, not an accident: (1) for any w in null(S), w^T S w = 0 implies (D^T w)^T (cov + s2 I)(D^T w) = 0 with cov + s2 I positive definite (s2 = 0.0112 from training replicates), so D^T w = 0 and the null-space component is annihilated by `cov @ D.T @ w` regardless of which solution is returned; (2) lstsq (gelsd, SVD) projects any round-off component of r outside range(S) away rather than amplifying it, and the non-zero singular values of S are bounded below by 14*s2 (the K_n Laplacian eigenvalue) — orders of magnitude above the rcond cutoff — so the result does not depend on BLAS pivot luck. The 34-test suite passes. Note also that the claim's proposed assertion `matrix_rank(S) == len(pairs)` would itself raise on every complete-graph support (13 != 91), so it is not a valid fix. No number in the <arm>@BLUP20 Setting B columns is at risk from this.
